chunks: And by this chain, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever performs ablution and perfects the ablution, and prays two Rak'at, completing their bowing and their prostrations, then sits and lauds Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and sends blessings upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), then asks Allah for his need, has indeed sought goodness in its habitats; and whoever seeks goodness in its habitats will not be unsuccessful.'

key_terms.صَلَّى عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Sent blessings upon the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended method for performing prayer to fulfill personal needs according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a structured spiritual protocol for Istikhara and general supplication, emphasizing that sincerity in ritual purity and prayer guarantees the acceptance of one's needs. It reflects the Shia emphasis on the efficacy of specific devotional acts when performed with presence of heart, linking physical preparation (Wudu) with spiritual focus (Salat) to ensure the petitioner does not return empty-handed.

en.hubeali: And by this chain, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al Hassan Bin Salih who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The one who performs Wuzu, so he perfects the Wuzu and prays two Rak’at of Salāt, completing their Rukūs and their Sajud (plural of Sajdah), then sits, so he Lauds upon Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic and sends Blessings upon Rasool-Allahsaww, then asks Allahazwj for his needs, so he has sought the goodness from its habitat; and the one who seeks the goodness in its habitat would never be unsuccessful’.
en.sarwar: 5. Through the same chain of narrators as the previous Hadith, it is narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from al- Hassan ibn Salih who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, say this. ‘One, for coming true of his wish, may take a proper Wudu’, perform two Rak‘at Salah (prayer) with complete Ruku‘ and sajdah. He then can sit and praises Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious. He then can say, “Allahumma Salli ‘Ala Muhammad wa ‘Ali Muhammad (O Allah grant Muhammad and his family a compensation worthy of their serving Your cause).” Thereafter ask Allah for his needs, he has asked Him for needs in a time of a good chance for acceptance, in which case one is not deprived of coming true of his wish.’”
